summary: Proceed as rewrite stage 1. The wgmma register-A swap-AB design suits the bs=128/256 verify shapes, where Marlin is 94-95% of the shape at about 3-4.5x the floor, and no landed hypothesis confounds it. One blocking arithmetic error must be fixed before implementing: as written, the N=64 and N=128 stage tables exceed Hopper's 227 KB of shared memory. The kernel would then fall back to master on the judge, and the run would measure nothing.
justification: Mechanism is sound. FINDINGS gives Marlin 316.1 us at bs=128 and 490.2 us at bs=256 (94.0% / 95.2% of the shape) against 101.3 / 108.9 us floors, and every lever tried inside Marlin (block_size_m picks, fp32-reduce off, atomic add, workspace) is exhausted or within CI, so replacing the GEMM pair is the remaining lever at these shapes. Specific checks: (1) The wgmma m64nNk16 register-A fragment is four stacked m16n8k16 A fragments, one per warp, and the accumulator gives each thread rows lane/4 and lane/4+8 of its warp's 16 rows. So the 8-row gate/up interleave really does put gate and up of the same intermediate column in one thread, and silu*up fusion needs no exchange. Correct. (2) Register budget: setmaxnreg 40x128 + 232x256 = 64512 <= 65536. OK. (3) Bytes in flight at 48 KB/SM is enough for M3 (2.9 TB/s) but not for ~4.5 TB/s. (4) Dequant ALU at ~1 op/weight is ~30-50 us per pass over the touched bank. That is acceptable only if it overlaps the stream, which stage 1 does only through async wgmma, as the file admits. BLOCKING DEFECT: the smem table. N=128, BK=128 is 9 KB weight + 32 KB slab = 41 KB/stage, and 6 stages = 246 KB. N=64, BK=256 is 18 KB + 32 KB = 50 KB/stage, and 5 stages = 250 KB. Both exceed the 227 KB opt-in limit, not just the self-imposed 200 KB. Only N<=32 fits (N=32: 34 KB x 6 = 204 KB; N=16: 26 KB x 6 = 156 KB). At bs=256 (and for hot experts at bs=128) chunks of 64-128 rows are common, so cudaFuncSetAttribute fails and the whole path falls back to master: a wasted run. Fix: N=128 at 4-5 stages of BK=128, or BK=64 with 8-10 stages, and N=64 at 4 stages of BK=256. Accept less weight in flight at large N, which is fine because the MMA per weight byte is higher there. Add a Python-side assert of per-bucket smem <= 227 KB before compiling. SECOND DESIGN COST (stage-2 note, not blocking): with a 128-row weight tile, the token slab is re-read from L2 once per weight tile: 64 times for w13 and 32 times for w2. At N=128 the slab is ~3.5x the weight bytes per K. Rough L2 activation traffic at bs=256 is ~300 MB (w13) + ~150 MB (w2), the same order as the 523 MB HBM stream. That probably caps a stage-1 result above the ~1.5x-floor target (~165 us) though not above M3. A 256-row weight tile per CTA (each consumer doing two m64 sets), or N=256 for hot experts, halves this. WEAKEST LINK: the compute argument is internally inconsistent. The file says ~350-450 local routes at bs=256 but 70-90 us of MMA at peak. 400 routes x 50.3M MACs x 2 = ~40 GFLOP = ~41 us at 989 TF. 70-90 us implies ~700-900 routes, which matches bs=128's stated ~40 us at peak only if bs=128 has ~400 routes. Either way the case for wgmma stands: even 41-60 us of MMA at mma.sync's ~60% of peak plus serialized dequant eats most of a 109 us budget. But the route count should be pinned from the profile/log so that M3's 220 us target is grounded. Expected directions are consistent with TASK: only bs=128/256 scored shapes change, the bs<128 controls are byte-for-byte master, and the 5 tests include bs=257 and the skewed bs=128 on the new path.
confounders: None from landed hypotheses: the landed list for master's submission.py is empty in this review's input, so no landed patch shares the area.

Master's block_size_m two-smaller pick at num_tokens >= 128 (16 at bs=128, 32 at bs=256) defines the incumbent Marlin rows (316.1 / 490.2 us). The new path bypasses it with block 16 plus on-device chunking. This is not a confound because the hypothesis is judged on its own kernel rows against those incumbent rows, but the comparison is against the tuned Marlin, not SGLang's pick.

In-flight align-parallel-per-expert-verify (running) changes the bs>=128 align. If it lands before this is implemented, the align row and its outputs change under this path. The file correctly reads only (sorted_ids, block_experts, n_padded) at block 16 and asks for the align row to be read separately, so no ambiguity in the replaced rows.
interference: No companion is warranted. This is kind: rewrite, judged on its own replaced rows (gather + w13 + w2 vs the Marlin pair + act_and_mul) per shape in top_kernels, not on the headline, and no landed hypothesis touches the same kernels, launch sequence or numerical path. An ab-revert has nothing to revert. An ab-tune of master's block_size_m pick is moot because the new path does not use it. A control isolating the fused silu or the split-K for w2 at bs=128 would cost a run to separate a few us out of ~300, and that is exactly what stage 2's profile-driven tuning does. The only thing that would make this single result uninterpretable is a silent fallback to master. The fix is the smem-table correction and the loud PATH CHOSEN / per-bucket smem log already specified, not a companion run.
rules_flags: Low: the w13 epilogue applies silu(gate)*up to fp32 accumulators without first rounding gate/up to bf16. SGLang materializes cache1 (gate/up) in BF16 before act_and_mul ('BF16 wherever SGLang's kernel keeps BF16'). Fusion with a higher-precision intermediate is very likely acceptable, and the bs<=32 sibling does the same, but rounding gate and up to bf16 before silu costs one cvt per pair and makes it literally compliant and closer to Marlin parity in the self-check. Recommend doing it.
OK: the NVFP4 stays NVFP4 (a permuted copy with a byte-exact round-trip assert per expert), dequant is in-kernel, and accumulation is fp32 with BF16 h and y stored.

OK: no host syncs in kernel_fn. Work items are built on device from block_experts/n_padded, the branch is on num_tokens and a prepare flag only, and ticket reset by the last arriver is graph-replay safe. Assert tickets are 0 after the self-check, as planned.

OK: xs/h_sorted/partials and the tensor maps over them are prepare-allocated scratch, overwritten every call, and nothing input-derived persists. Zero-initialize them in prepare anyway. Stale rows past n_padded only reach masked token columns, because swap-AB keeps columns independent, but zeroed scratch removes any NaN-pattern doubt.
OK: the self-check uses synthetic routings and real weights in prepare, untimed, with no reference import. Keep the fp32 e2m1/e4m3 decode written locally, as stated.
open_questions: Fix the per-bucket smem table: N=64 (5 x 50 KB = 250 KB) and N=128 (6 x 41 KB = 246 KB) exceed 227 KB. What stage counts are chosen, and does the Python side assert the budget before compiling?

The TMA box dims are fixed per tensor map: is one CUtensorMap encoded per N bucket per scratch (4 x 2 = 8 maps)? Is BK=128/256 at SWIZZLE_128B (64 bf16 inner box) issued as 2-4 boxes per stage, with each slab stage base 1024 B aligned for the wgmma descriptor?

How is cuTensorMapEncodeTiled reached: a host function in the TU with extra_ldflags=['-lcuda'], or cuda-python? Is it confirmed available in the judge image? muse_attention_decode's _build_splitkv used load_inline but, from its flags, not the driver API.

The L2 policy contradicts the reuse plan. The weight record is loaded with evict_first, yet items are ordered so a hot expert's second chunk 'hits L2' on the same tile. Use evict_normal (or evict_last) when an expert has more than one chunk, or have one item cover all of an expert's chunks with multiple accumulators so the tile is dequantized once.
What is the item-to-CTA assignment: static stride or an atomic work counter? Item costs vary by N bucket (16 to 128), so a static stride can leave a tail of several items at ~10-12 items per CTA.
Chunk formation: 'every CTA loads block_experts and forms chunks' over up to 160 blocks. If one thread scans serially it costs ~2-4 us per launch, twice. Use a warp-ballot/prefix scan.

The w2 epilogue scatters to cache3[sorted_ids[slot], :]. In swap-AB a thread's fragment is strided along H per token, so this needs the same smem-staged transpose (stmatrix .trans) as w13 to get 256 B coalesced row writes. Please specify it.
Pin the busiest-GPU local route counts at bs=128 and bs=256 (the file says ~350-450 at bs=256 but 70-90 us of MMA, which implies ~800). Logging items per shape from the profile run would ground M3.
